title: Race Condition — Evacuation Twin
summary: A fork of the Race Condition multi-agent marathon simulation, repurposed as a location-swappable civilian evacuation twin for planning and education, with a DTSF twin backend and browser-run city scenarios.

contribution.roleNote: Modifies Race Condition (GoogleCloudPlatform/race-condition) by Casey West and the Race Condition team at Google; derivative work under Apache 2.0.

narrative.problem: Upstream Race Condition models thousands of autonomous agents moving along a route through a real 3D city. Civilian evacuation is structurally the same problem — many people, imperfect information, shared routes, bottlenecks, stopping points and a clock — but needs location-specific scenarios grounded in open data rather than a marathon.
narrative.decision: Each scenario is opt-in through a ?scenario=<id> URL parameter and a pure-data pack (building footprints, routes, POIs, damage) drawn by a GLB-less schematic renderer, so the upstream Vegas marathon stays render-identical and the static build runs on GitHub Pages with no backend or API keys.
narrative.tradeoff: Pure-data scenarios run offline at no cost, but they are rendered schematically and are not yet driven by the live multi-agent engine: the Go gateway and ADK agents still run the Vegas marathon, and the DTSF twin replays a deterministic trajectory instead of the realtime WebSocket stream.
narrative.limitation: Evacuation behaviour in the backend is largely an RFC: scenarios are not wired into the live engine, cohort movement and hazard-aware routing are parameters rather than agent behaviour, the DTSF twin control plane is open work, building heights are hashed, and the NYC Marathon route is about 88% of the official distance.
narrative.caveat: Planning and education exercise over open and synthetic data: zones, exits, corridors and demographics are illustrative and building heights are hashed. Not operational; it must not be used to locate or interdict people.
